earlier_scan.source_named: Roberts, David. 2011. Grammaire kabiyè: une esquisse (SIL) — full grammar sketch with phonology; Kabiyè is described as tonal (Wikipedia phonology section read: tone only, no stress statement found).

new_statements.quote: Admittedly, since a moraic account prohibits downstep occurring between two moras with no intervening consonant, one might legitimately ask why weightless consonant onsets should participate in the placement of downstep. The usual evidence for this comes from stress assignment patterns, where the presence of a consonant onset causes a syllable to attract stress, but this is not the case in Kabiye phonology because stress is not phonemic. [fn. 4, p. 7:] In some languages with phonemic stress, it may be necessary to state "below the level of the foot", but this is not the case in Kabiye.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Kabiyé is a two-tone language (H, L; Roberts 2022 p. 1 citing Lébikaza 1999: 183). Stress is stated to be non-phonemic; no position for word stress is described anywhere in the accessible literature, and the tonal literature (Roberts 2003, 2008, 2019, 2021, 2022) never invokes stress or prominence as a factor. No fixed or predictable stress position can be assigned from the sources read.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any source read.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the statement is a passing remark inside an argument about moraic tone-bearing units, not a dedicated stress section.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level phonology (tone assignment to moras/syllables in nouns and verbs); the remark concerns phonemic (contrastive) stress, and says nothing about phonetic prominence in citation forms or phrases.
new_statements.identity_note: Sources describe Kabiyé proper (kbp, kabi1261) as spoken in the Kara region of Togo; Roberts' data are from his own fieldwork with L1 speakers; no dialect specified beyond the standard variety used for the orthography. The earlier scan's named source 'Roberts 2011, Grammaire kabiyè: une esquisse (SIL)' could not be confirmed to exist.
